In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a hollow shaft stirrer allows to eliminate the limiting step of the gas to liquid transfer during hydrate crystallisation.
the use of a hollow shaft stirrer is a very good solution to enhance the gas to liquid mass transfer during CO2 hydrate crystallization, in particular in the presence of a high gas to liquid ratio.
the CO2 hydrate crystallization process is controlled by mass transfer in the liquid phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization driving force is a key parameter for CO2 hydrate crystallization.
the CO2 hydrate crystallization rate can be enhanced by the gas to liquid transfer rate increase, and that it can be obtained by the hollow shaft stirrer use.
we have developed a new experimental device allowing us to measure in real-time and in situ the gas/liquid transfer rate during hydrate crystallisation.

the gas to liquid transfer enhancement is a promising approach to enhance hydrate slurry production rate.
